title: Architect Evidence Flipbook — Sprint Draft
summary: Working slide pack aimed at platform architects and integration teams. Presents compact, data-forward evidence (benchmarks, fallback economics, rollout patterns) to shorten technical qualification and accelerate pilot commitments. This is intentionally terse — each slide is a single evidence nugget + one recommended call-to-action.
objectives: Give platform architects quick, verifiable datapoints they can take to procurement and infra teams
Provide structured rebuttals to common technical objections (latency, isolation, model drift)
Offer reproducible micro-experiments (pilot checklist) to de-risk first 30 days
Standardize CTAs that map to our pricing and Dedicated/Private packaging
key_messages: Redwood optimizes for predictable per-token economics without sacrificing tail latency
We provide fallbacks and model routing to keep critical paths online during capacity events
Dedicated pools give single-tenant throughput guarantees with measurable cost breakpoints vs bursty hosted usage
Private deployments keep control plane and data paths inside customer VPCs with optional on-prem artifacts
slide_outlines: Cover: title + one-line value prop for architects
Why Evidence Matters: typical infra buyer checklist and how we map to it
Latency evidence: 95th/99th tail on common seq lengths (100, 512) across t4/gpu64 targets
Cost per 1M tokens: hosted vs dedicated vs quantized private — three scenarios with simple math
Fallback resilience: routing policy example and observed failover times from production drills
Pilot playbook (30-day): infra pre-req, sample payloads, eval prompts, telemetry hooks
Rollout pattern: canary -> weighted rollout -> automatic fallback policy example
Security + compliance items: KMS/HSM, audit trail example, SOC/ISO pointers
Field checklist for SEs: questions to ask and artifacts to collect in first meeting
Appendix: benchmark methodology and links to raw logs / reproducible scripts
rebuttals_snippets: Objection: 'Hosted latency spikes are unacceptable' — Snippet: show 99th percentile and explain burst pool + KV prefix caching that keeps cold-starts under our SLA in 98% of request distributions
Objection: 'Costs will balloon with usage' — Snippet: show cost-per-token inflection point where Dedicated beats hosted, include committed-throughput vs burst assumptions
Objection: 'We need air-gapped option' — Snippet: summarize Private on-prem package, expected integration effort (2-4 weeks), and sample SOW line items
Objection: 'Model quality drifts' — Snippet: outline eval harness + rollback policy; show how quality regressions trigger canary rollback and notification
example_kpis: Target: P95 request latency < 120ms for seq<=128 on Dedicated X-1 pool
Cost goal: < $6 per 1M tokens for high-volume reranking workloads under committed throughput
Reliability: automated fallback engaged < 1% of requests during capacity events
Pilot success: end-to-end latency and accuracy parity within 10% of PoC baseline within 30 days
field_play_scripts: 60s opener: restate top infra concern, present 2 evidence slides (latency table + cost breakpoint), ask which of the two is the gating concern
3min demo snippet: run sample prompt against hosted baseline, show KV cache effect by re-sending prefixes, flip to dedicated config and show throughput improvement
Close-for-pilot: confirm infra contacts, propose 30-day pilot scope, request access to 1 sample raw workload and a DB dump for data residency review
pilot_checklist: Access: service account + IP allowlist + sample traffic pattern (CSV)
Telemetry: enable token-level logging and route to customer Grafana/dedicated export
SLOs & Alerts: define 95/99 latency targets and error budget
Data: confirm PII redaction needs and KMS configuration
Rollback: test canary rollback and fallback to smaller model variant

draft_notes: This pack intentionally avoids marketing jargon. Focus on numbers and small reproducible tasks. Next steps: run one more 99th-tail test on our smallest dedicated SKU and update slide 3. Reach out in #g2m-evidence if you need access to the benchmark cluster. Keep this draft lean — aim for 8 slides total in the first publishable version. Potential follow-ups: tenant isolation deep-dive and a one-pager for procurement covering commercial breakpoints.
